answer: A durable defence ties each identity to a slowly grown record of verified work, like a garden that cannot be faked overnight. New agents start with limited rights and earn trust only when independent peers confirm completed tasks; each confirmation becomes a costly, public signal that is hard to mass-produce. If one identity misbehaves, its whole history is pruned, so creating many cheap copies, timber cut without roots, yields no advantage, because only rooted, witnessed history unlocks higher-value work.
